messages.content: Find carbonate sites near the rover.

I'll search for carbonate evidence near the rover.Two spots are close and rover-confirmed: one about 1.4 km away (samples Salette and Coulettes) and a larger one about 1.5 km out (samples Robine and Malay), both gentle ground at 5 to 6 degrees. Everything else is much farther (6.7 km and up) and only detected from orbit by CRISM on MRO, at strong-orbital tier — the caveat is that CRISM pixels are 36 m, so near a boundary the tier may belong to the neighbouring pixel. Note the rover confirmation positions are derived to within 10 to 50 m, and this is a synthetic test site.

Want me to plan a drive to the nearer confirmed patch?
What time is it at Jezero right now?

It's night on sol 2040: about 04:36 local true solar time (05:02 on the mission mean clock), with the sun 16.4 degrees below the horizon. Sunrise is at 05:47 LTST. (Geometric direct sun only — dusty twilight isn't modelled, so it isn't pitch dark.)
Back to the carbonate spots: go to the first one.
